records.title: How it works
records.subtitle: How Rapi Mock reads resources, keys and links off an OpenAPI spec, and what the three labels mean.
records.content: An OpenAPI spec describes operations. It never says "these five operations are about the same pet". Rapi Mock works that out, and tells you how sure it is. From paths and schemas to resources These three paths: share a schema and a path shape, so they become one resource , Pet. From that the mock derives: - The key : the path parameter matched to a field, {petId} to id. - What each operation does : list, create, read, update, patch or delete. - Links : a field such as ownerId points at the Owner resource, so seeded pets belong to seeded owners. - Parents : a comment created at /articles/{slug}

records.title: Introduction
records.subtitle: What Rapi Mock is, what it is for, and how it differs from the in-browser mock.
records.content: Rapi Mock is a mock server for the APIs you describe with OpenAPI. Give it a spec and it answers every operation over HTTP, so a frontend, a test suite or another service can call your API before it exists. It is the rapidoc mock command of the RapiDoc CLI, backed by the @rapidoc/mock package. What it does - Answers every operation from the spec's examples, or with data generated from its schemas. - Validates requests against the spec: a bad request gets a 400 with the problems listed. - Checks tokens : OAuth and bearer tokens are verified against your issuer, with the operation's scopes. - Ke

records.title: What it does
records.subtitle: Introduction
records.content: - Answers every operation from the spec's examples, or with data generated from its schemas. - Validates requests against the spec: a bad request gets a 400 with the problems listed. - Checks tokens : OAuth and bearer tokens are verified against your issuer, with the operation's scopes. - Keeps state , with --stateful: it works out the resources in your spec, starts with generated records, and remembers what you create, change and delete. - Shows you what it holds : the Mock UI lists the records

records.title: What it is not
records.subtitle: Introduction
records.content: - Not a copy of your backend. It knows what the spec says: shapes, required fields, which paths belong together. It does not know your business rules, such as "an order can't ship before it is paid". - Not a database. Data lives in memory and starts fresh on every run. - Not for production traffic. Its control endpoints are open by design. Run it on a developer's machine or in CI.

records.title: The state document
records.subtitle: Control API
records.content: snapshot returns it and restore takes it: - A restore replaces every resource of the APIs it names; a resource it leaves out becomes empty. Other APIs are left alone. - A document that is wrong changes nothing. - A record that lives under a parent without having a field for it carries the parent in $parents. Keep that entry when you restore.

records.title: Picking a response
records.subtitle: Choose which documented response the mock returns, with the Prefer header.
records.content: Clients choose which documented response they get with a Prefer header: | Header | Effect | | :--- | :--- | | Prefer: code=404 | The documented 404 response (else 4XX, else default). | | Prefer: example=empty | The example named empty. | | Prefer: dynamic=true | Generated data, even when the spec has an example. | The response's Preference-Applied header tells you which preferences were used. With --stateful, a request with Prefer: code= or Prefer: example= gets that response as the spec writes it, and nothing is read or stored. This is how a test forces an error path.

records.title: Tokens and scopes
records.subtitle: How Rapi Mock enforces each operation's security, with real token checks against your issuer.
records.content: Security is enforced per operation, as the spec declares it. - OAuth 2, OpenID Connect and HTTP bearer : with --issuer, the token must be a JWT signed by that issuer, unexpired and for the --audience, or the request gets 401. It must also grant the operation's scopes in its scope, scp or permissions claim, or the request gets 403 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient scope". - Without --issuer , any bearer token is accepted. The mock says so when it starts. - API key and HTTP Basic : the credential must be present. - security: [] : open. Security is checked before the request is va

records.title: What it answers
records.subtitle: Where Rapi Mock's responses come from, and how requests are validated.
records.content: - Examples first. An operation's response example is returned when the spec has one; otherwise data is generated from the schema, respecting formats, patterns, enums and ranges. Generated data is the same on every run (change it with --seed). - Requests are validated. Parameters and JSON, form and multipart bodies are checked against the spec. A bad request gets 400 with the list of problems (422 when the operation documents 422 and not 400). - OpenAPI 3.2 methods. QUERY operations and those under additionalOperations (PURGE, COPY, LINK, ...) are served and validated like the others, and pass

records.title: An example written the wrong way
records.subtitle: What it answers
records.content: Some specs put a named example under example, where it belongs under examples: The mock returns the value under the name, not the wrapper, when the response schema confirms it. rapidoc lint reports it as example-named-map. With --stateful, operations that fit a resource are answered from stored records. See Keeping state.

records.subtitle: Which kinds of API Rapi Mock keeps state for with no configuration, and which need a few lines.
records.content: Rapi Mock reads the data model off your spec. How much it finds depends on how the API is written. This page says plainly where it works and where it needs help. Works with no configuration APIs where: - a record has its own path, with its id in it: /pets/{petId}; - the key is a field at the top of the record: id, slug, username; - the collection is at the path above: /pets. The list may be a bare array, sit under data, items or results, in a page object under values, or under a property named after the resource (load balancers). records.title: Not supported yet
records.subtitle: API styles
records.content: - One-of-a-kind records , read and written at a fixed path, such as /settings/vacation. They are answered as a plain mock. - Swagger 2.0. The mock reads OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2. Convert a 2.0 spec first. - APIs that are not resource-style , such as chat.postMessage. These are answered as a plain mock throughout, which is the right outcome: there are no resources to keep.

records.title: Keeping state
records.subtitle: With --stateful, Rapi Mock remembers what you create, change and delete.
records.content: By default every call is answered on its own: a POST returns a made-up record, and the next GET doesn't know about it. With --stateful the mock keeps data, like the real server would: - It works out the data model from the spec. Paths such as /pets and /pets/{petId} that share a schema become one resource, with its key and its links to other resources. How it works has the details. - It starts with data. Each resource gets 10 records (--rows). See Seed data. - Writes are kept. A create stores a record, an update or delete changes it, and reads and lists return what is stored. - Lists filter an

records.title: What a new record gets
records.subtitle: Keeping state
records.content: Fields the caller can't send, or left out, are filled the way a server would: an id, timestamps set to now, lists empty, counts at zero. A key the path expects as a number is a number.

records.title: When a record is missing
records.subtitle: Keeping state
records.content: A read, update or delete of a record that isn't there returns the spec's own 404 response when it documents one.

records.title: Sessions
records.subtitle: Give each test its own copy of the data with the X-Mock-Session header.
records.content: Send an X-Mock-Session header to get your own copy of the data. Tests that run at the same time then never see each other's changes: - A session starts as a copy of the seed data, made when it first writes. - Requests without the header share the default data. - The control endpoints follow the header too: a reset or a read of the state with X-Mock-Session works on that session only. Any value works as a session id. A test's own name is a good one.

records.title: Tests in any language
records.subtitle: Prepare and check Rapi Mock's data over HTTP, from pytest, JUnit, Go or anything else.
records.content: The mock has its own endpoints under / mock, beside the APIs. A test in any language uses them over HTTP: wait until the mock is ready, reset the data, act through the API, then check what was stored. The pattern Tests that run in parallel Give each test its own session, and it never sees another test's data. No reset is needed between them: Starting from your own data Load the records a test needs, in place of the generated ones: POST / mock/snapshot returns the current records in the same shape, to save and load again later. In CI Start the mock in the background, wait for it, run the tests:

records.title: The pattern
records.subtitle: Tests in any language
records.content: ```python

records.title: pytest
records.subtitle: Tests in any language
records.content: import requests MOCK = "http://localhost:4010" def setup function(): requests.post(f"{MOCK}/ mock/reset") back to the seed data def test adopting a pet(): pet = requests.post(f"{MOCK}/openapi/pets", json={"name": "Biscuit"}).json() requests.patch(f"{MOCK}/openapi/pets/{pet['id']}", json={"status": "sold"}) stored = requests.get(f"{MOCK}/ mock/state/openapi/Pet/{pet['id']}").json() assert stored["status"] == "sold" ```
